newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WESTPAC TO TRIAL MONDEX IN AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: WESTPAC TO TRIAL MONDEX IN AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp on Monday launched Australia's first trial of the Mondex electronic cash technology.
The trial is being conducted at a Westpac staff cafetaria in suburban Sydney and involves about 200 staff.
Westpac said the trial will allow a staff member to buy his or her own lunch by inserting their Mondex smart card into the merchant's smart card wallet or point-of-sale terminal.
"They can also spend and receive electronic cash person-to-person, using a Mondex electronic wallet," Westpac General Manager of Card Products Rob Bishop said in a statement.
Bishop told reporters that wide-scale commercialisation of a Westpac-issued Mondex card will occur in the second half of 1998.

He said currently the trial of the Mondex technology only involves limited uses such as storing credit on the card, which can then be used to transfer value to other Mondex cards or at terminals point of sale.

When the card is eventually released in the second half of 1998, Mondex customers will be using a card that will have the MULTOS chip card platform enabling such uses as paying for airline tickets and telephone bills, Bishop said.
"It is a very early stage of something that is going to be a pretty big deal to us," Bishop said.
Bishop said clearing and settlement is a major ongoing cost fort any bank operating an electronic cash system which is avoided using the Mondex technology.
"The trial will allow us to become familiar with Mondex technology and gain operational experience internally before finalising when and how to introduce it to market," he said.

The concept is owned by Mondex International Ltd, an independent global payments company owned by MasterCard International and 26 other major companies in North America, Europe, southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand.
